title: The Branch of Jesse
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Context of Devastation
subpoints: Historical background of the divided kingdoms of Israel and Judah
The impending judgment from Assyria and Babylon
The imagery of cut trees and wasteland in Isaiah 10

outline.title: The Emergence of the Branch
subpoints: The rod from the stem of Jesse as a sign of hope
The indwelling of the Spirit of the Lord
The character of the Messiah: wisdom, counsel, and fear of the Lord

outline.title: The Righteous Reign
subpoints: Judgment based on righteousness and equity, not human perception
The defeat of the wicked through the word of the Messiah
Righteousness and faithfulness as the belt of the King

outline.title: The Restoration of Creation
subpoints: Peace among predatory and prey animals
Safety for children in the presence of danger
The earth filled with the knowledge of the Lord

outline.title: The Banner to the Gentiles
subpoints: The root of Jesse standing as a banner to the nations
The glorious resting place of the King

summary:
This sermon, delivered during the Advent season, explores Isaiah 11:1-10 as a central Messianic prophecy within the broader context of Isaiah's warnings of judgment. The speaker identifies chapters 7 through 12 of Isaiah as a 'Gospel according to Isaiah,' highlighting how prophecies of Christ are woven into messages of divine judgment against the unfaithful kingdoms of Israel and Judah. The historical backdrop of Assyrian and Babylonian invasions serves to emphasize the severity of the coming devastation, setting the stage for the hope found in the 'Branch of Jesse.'

The message focuses on the person and work of Jesus Christ, affirming the New Testament's interpretation of this Old Testament text, particularly through Paul's citation in Romans 15. The sermon details the attributes of the Messiah, who is empowered by the Spirit of the Lord and characterized by wisdom, understanding, and a deep reverence for God. Unlike human rulers who judge by appearance, this King judges with righteousness and equity, bringing peace and restoration to a broken world.

Finally, the sermon highlights the eschatological hope of a restored creation where natural enemies coexist in peace, symbolizing the comprehensive renewal that comes through the Messiah. This 'root of Jesse' is presented not only as a savior for Israel but as a banner to the Gentiles, pointing to the universal scope of Christ's ministry and the ultimate glory of His reign.
